Tracing this now. Initial triage notes:
- I reproduced the error locally against a proxied stream when the client sends header metadata > ~2KB. The Node SDK v1.4.2 streaming parser appears to mishandle chunk boundaries when headers are split across TCP chunks by some proxies.
- Behavior: partial header lines are dropped instead of buffered which causes the server to reject the frame with a parse error. That explains the sudden jump after upgrade (parser behavior changed in 1.4.x).
- Workaround: set the client option "forceSingleHeaderWrite: true" or downgrade to 1.3.9. The option prevents splitting header writes at the client level.

Attaching sdk_debug_trace.txt which contains local reproduction output and stack traces. I'm starting a small patch to the parser to buffer across chunk boundaries (will PR if confirmed).

Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: sudden spike in stream failures after SDK upgrade — follow up & patch

Update for OmniaHealth and internal team:

Root cause: Connor confirmed that the Node client streaming parser introduced in v1.4.0 changed how it handled incoming header boundaries. When a proxy splits a multipart header across TCP chunks, the parser sometimes failed to buffer the partial header which resulted in header truncation and stream parse errors. The edge case manifests only when header metadata exceeds ~2KB and when intermediate proxies re-chunk writes.

Action taken:
- Engineering created a patch to buffer header fragments across chunk boundaries and added regression tests for proxied re-chunking. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/422 (attached).
- Patch is in review; we will cut v1.4.3 with the fix and a focused canary tomorrow morning.
- Mitigation for OmniaHealth: keep clients on 1.3.9 (rollback) OR enable the client-level flag "forceSingleHeaderWrite: true" as a temporary measure (best-effort).

Proposed business response:
- Offer a one-month credit (proposed 10% of July invoice) contingent on leadership approval.
- Provide a post-incident report with timeline, root cause, and steps to prevent regressions.

Next steps: Connor will schedule a quick technical call with OmniaHealth engineers to validate the patch in their staging proxy topology. Rishi / Marissa — please confirm whether the proposed credit is acceptable so I can confirm during the exec call.

Thanks everyone — we'll keep the channel updated.

Stephanie Nguyen
